subtopics.title: Momentum and Newton's Second Law in Momentum Form

questions.question: Linear momentum is defined as:
options: The energy an object has because of its motion
The product of an object's mass and its velocity
The force needed to stop an object
The product of an object's mass and its acceleration

questions.question: A 1 500 kg minibus travels at 25 m·s⁻¹ east. Its momentum is:
A 0,4 kg ball hits a wall at 12 m·s⁻¹ and rebounds at 9 m·s⁻¹. Taking toward the wall as positive, its change in momentum is:
Newton's second law in terms of momentum states that the net force equals:
options: The rate of change of momentum
The total momentum of the system
The change in momentum multiplied by the time taken

questions.question: The impulse-momentum theorem states that FnetΔt equals:
options: ½mv², the kinetic energy of the object
mΔv, the change in momentum of the object
ma, the net force on the object
mgh, the potential energy of the object

questions.question: A 0,06 kg tennis ball arrives at 25 m·s⁻¹ and is returned straight back at 35 m·s⁻¹. The magnitude of the impulse on the ball is:
If that impulse of 3,6 N·s is delivered in 0,005 s, the average net force on the ball is:
A crumple zone protects passengers in a crash because it:
options: Reduces the change in momentum of the car
Increases the time over which the momentum changes, reducing the net force

questions.question: The principle of conservation of linear momentum applies to a system that is:
options: Isolated — no net external force acts on it

questions.question: During a collision, the forces the two objects exert on each other cannot change the total momentum because they are:
options: Equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, acting inside the system

questions.question: A 6 kg launcher at rest fires a 0,03 kg dart at 200 m·s⁻¹. The launcher's recoil velocity is:
After the launcher fires, the dart and launcher have:

subtopics.title: Collisions in One Dimension — Elastic or Inelastic

questions.question: A 3 kg trolley at 4 m·s⁻¹ hits a stationary 2 kg trolley and they couple. Their common velocity is:
An elastic collision is one in which:
In the trolley collision, kinetic energy drops from 24 J to 14,4 J. The correct conclusion is:
options: The calculation must be wrong, since energy cannot disappear
The collision was inelastic — 9,6 J became heat, sound and deformation

questions.question: Which quantity is conserved in BOTH elastic and inelastic collisions in an isolated system?

subtopics.title: Moving Oomph — Why Mass and Speed Both Count

questions.question: A shot-put is harder to catch than a netball at the same speed because it has:
options: More momentum, because it has more mass

questions.question: A slow cement truck can carry more momentum than a fast pellet because:
options: Momentum is mass times velocity, and its huge mass outweighs its low speed

questions.question: A ball that bounces off a wall changes its momentum MORE than one that stops dead because:
options: The wall pushes only on bouncing balls
It must lose all its forward momentum AND gain momentum in the opposite direction

questions.question: An egg thrown at a duvet survives while one thrown at a wall breaks. The duvet:
options: Reduces the egg's change in momentum
Stretches the stopping time, so the force on the egg is smaller

questions.question: In every impulse safety question, the quantity that stays FIXED during the stop is:
Which of the following works on a DIFFERENT principle from the other three?
options: A gravel run-off bed stopping a runaway truck
A gymnast bending the knees on landing
A crumple zone folding in a crash
A seatbelt stopping a passenger from continuing forward

questions.question: The complete explanation for any impulse safety device has three steps, in this order:
options: The device is soft; the crash is slower; the person is safer
Force is smaller; time is longer; momentum change is fixed
Momentum change is fixed; the time is increased; therefore the force is smaller
Energy is absorbed; momentum is destroyed; force disappears

questions.question: A loaded trolley with 12 units of momentum latches onto a stationary trolley. Just after the crash, the pair's total momentum is:
options: 6 units, because it is shared between two trolleys
12 units, shared over the combined mass
24 units, because there are now two trolleys

questions.question: Momentum is conserved during the crash because the trolleys:
options: Only exert equal and opposite forces on each other, inside the system
Are made of the same material
Move too fast for friction to act

questions.question: Trolleys that latch together after a collision always give:
options: An inelastic collision — some kinetic energy is lost
A collision where momentum is not conserved

questions.question: The only valid way to decide whether a collision is elastic is to:
options: Check whether the objects bounced apart
Calculate total kinetic energy before and after and compare
